D-statistics (ABBA-BABA) are used to test for introgression. Specifically the
test operates by assigning ancestral (`A`) and derived (`B`) alleles, and checking
if there is an excess of ABBA or BABA patterns given a tree of `(((P1, P2), P3), O)`
where `O` is the outgroup. ABBA patterns indicate P2 and P3 have an excess of 
shared alleles, while BABA patterns result when P1 and P3 have an excess. If
there were no introgression, we'd expect ABBA and BABA patterns to occur equally
frequently (reflecting ILS and the like).

ƒ~d~ statistics are a variant of D-statistics, suitable for use with windowed
data. Here, we explore ƒ~d~ results relative to d~XY~ and see what the
relationship is. The expectation is that introgression would result in high ƒ~d~
within a window and low d~XY~.

Data for this analysis were not only filtered on the 10\% usable data that
we use in the diversity statistics, but also ensuring there are adequate SNPs
in the window ($\geq$200) to accurately estimate the statistics. We've also applied
the chromosome 2 mask to this data to minimise the impact of the misassembly in
that region.

```{r load-data}
# ƒd
df_fd <- dir_ls(
    here("results", "04-treeness-introgression", "fd"),
    glob = "*clean*.csv"
) |>
    read_csv(col_types = cols(), id = "tree") |>
    mutate(tree = str_extract(basename(tree), "H.*MGR")) |>
    filter(
        # No excess of shared derived alleles - making no assumption that introgression
        # is not occurring, simply removing to prevent 0 becoming a hard-floor
        D > 0
    ) |>
    separate(col = tree, into = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "O"), remove = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
        scaffold = factor(str_remove(scaffold, "chr"), levels = 1:16),
        comparison = case_when(
            P2 == "HCU" & P3 == "HEL" ~ "HCU-HEL",
            P2 == "HCU" & P3 == "HMA" ~ "HCU-HMA",
            P2 == "HEL" & P3 == "HMA" ~ "HEL-HMA",
            
            P2 == "HEL" & P3 == "HCU" ~ "HCU-HEL",
            P2 == "HMA" & P3 == "HEL" ~ "HEL-HMA",
            P2 == "HMA" & P3 == "HCU" ~ "HCU-HMA",
            .default = "unknown"
        )
    )

df_fst_dxy <- read_csv(
    here("results", "03-diversity", "between", "clean-data.csv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:16))
```

## D-statitics tree

Here I'm creating the framework for the figure. We've ordered the *Hydrophis*
snakes according to the ASTRAL-III tree from our 2023 paper. This also corresponds
to the *Dmin* orientation reported by `dsuite dtrios`.

> (M. gracilis,(H. elegans,(H. curtus, H. major)));

```{r}
tree_astral <- ape::read.tree(text = "(((A,B),C),D);")
tree_astral$tip.label <- c("H. curtus\n(P2)", "H. major\n(P1)", "H. elegans\n(P3)", "M. gracilis\n(O)")
plot_tree_astral <- ggtree(
    tree_astral,
    size = 4,
    colour = "#495057"
) +
    layout_dendrogram() +
    scale_y_reverse() +
    geom_tiplab(
        angle = 0,
        vjust = 2,
        hjust = 0.5,
        offset = 0.1,
        size = 7,
        color = "#6c757d",
        fontface = "italic"
    ) +
    labs(tag = "A") +
    theme_tree2(
        axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = unit(c(1,1,1,1), "cm")
    )

# Annotating the root
root <- plot_tree_astral$data[plot_tree_astral$data$node == plot_tree_astral$data$parent, ]

plot_tree_astral <- plot_tree_astral + 
    annotate(
        "richtext", x = root$x, y = root$y,
        label = "*D* = 0.017; *f~4~*-ratio = 0.86%",
        vjust = -0.5, 
        hjust = 1.2,
        size = 6, 
        colour = "#6c757d",
        fill = NA, label.colour = NA
    )

plot_tree_astral
```


## d~XY~ vs ƒ~d~

If there is gene flow between the P3 and P2, we'd expect divergence statistics to
be low in the windows where introgression is high. Below we plot d~XY~ against
ƒ~d~.

Specifically, we're plotting the divergence statistics between *H. curtus* (P2)
and *H. elegans* (P3) against the ƒ~d~ results for the matching topology.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
df_dat <- df_fd |>
    filter(tree == "HMA-HCU-HEL-MGR") |>
    inner_join(
        df_fst_dxy, 
        by = join_by(
            scaffold == chromosome, 
            start == window_pos_1, 
            end == window_pos_2,
            comparison
        )
    )

# fd vs dxy coloured by fst

p_fd_dxy_fill_fst <- df_dat |>
    ggplot(aes(x = fd, y = avg_dxy)) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.15, size = 3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", fill = "grey40") +
    ggpubr::stat_cor(
        method = "spearman",

        label.y.npc = 0.1,

        size = 5
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
        expand = c(0, 0.01)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 0.01),
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "ƒ~d~", 
        y = "d~XY~",
        tag = "B"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
        axis.text = element_text(size = 16),

        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

p_fd_dxy_fill_fst
```

## Challeneges of ƒ~d~

As is reported in Martin et al. 2015, signals of high ƒ~d~ can be a product of
low d~XY~ rather than genuine introgression. Low d~XY~ can arise from a multitude
of scenarios - both stochastically or due to ancestral population structure. As
such, certain evolutionary histories can result in regions of low d~XY~ being
dense with ƒ~d~ outlier loci even though evolutionarily there has been no allele
sharing between focal populations.

While we do not have simulation data to establish what a null signal might look
like in these snake species, we can at least check what's going on. Above, we see
that ƒ~d~ is negatively correlated with d~XY~, which isn't unexpected, but needs
investigation to properly understand if there has been any allele sharing.

### Comparing d~XY~ in outlier ƒ~d~ windows to non-outlier windows

Below we're going to combine components of figure 4 and 5 from [Martin et al. (2015)][martin2015].
Using the same P2-P3 comparison, 100kb windows are labelled ƒ~d~-outliers if they
fall in the top 90th percentile. We then compare d~XY~ distributions between ƒ~d~
outliers and non-outliers, and calculate mean d~XY~ in outlier windows as a percentage
of mean d~XY~ in non-outlier windows (i.e. the background). 

If gene flow has occurred, mean d~XY~ of outlier windows a percentage of non-outlier
windows will be **low**. In the absence of gene flow, we expect the percentage to
be high. Martin et al. 2015 show that simulated scenarios where there is real
gene flow have quite a distribution of percentage values (across many simulations),
while ancestral structure and null scenarios show relatively high percentage values.

```{r}
tmp <- df_dat |> 
    mutate(
        fd_cutoff = quantile(fd, probs = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
        fd_outlier = fd >= fd_cutoff,
        .by = tree
    ) |>
    select(tree, scaffold, start, end, avg_dxy, fd_outlier) |>
    mutate(fd_outlier = ifelse(fd_outlier, "Outlier","Background"))

dxy_pct <- df_dat |> 
    mutate(
        fd_cutoff = quantile(fd, probs = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
        fd_outlier = fd >= fd_cutoff,
        .by = tree
    )  |>
    summarise(
        P2P3_dxy_outlier = mean(avg_dxy[fd_outlier], na.rm = TRUE),
        P2P3_dxy_nonoutlier = mean(avg_dxy[!fd_outlier], na.rm = TRUE),
        P2P3_dxy_effect = 100 * (P2P3_dxy_outlier / P2P3_dxy_nonoutlier),
        n_outlier = sum(fd_outlier, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_nonoutlier = sum(!fd_outlier, na.rm = TRUE),
        .by = tree
    )

means <- tmp |>
  summarise(mean_dxy = mean(avg_dxy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = fd_outlier)

pct_lab <- sprintf(
  "%.0f%% of background",
  100 * means$mean_dxy[means$fd_outlier == "Outlier"] /
    means$mean_dxy[means$fd_outlier == "Background"]
)
    
p_fd_outlier_pct <- tmp |>
    ggplot(aes(x = fd_outlier, y = avg_dxy)) +
    geom_hline(
        yintercept = dxy_pct$P2P3_dxy_effect / 100 * 0.01, 
        linetype = "dashed", 
        linewidth = 1,
        colour = "#D72000FF"
    ) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
    stat_summary(
        fun = mean,
        geom = "point",
        shape = 23,
        size = 2.5,
        fill = "#D72000FF"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 0.01),
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5),
        sec.axis = sec_axis(
            transform = ~ . / 0.01,
            labels = scales::label_percent(),
            breaks = seq.int(0, 1, 0.1),
            name = "Outlier to background P2-P3 d~XY~ (%)"
        )
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "ƒ~d~ window type", 
        y = "d~XY~",
        tag = "C"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
        axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 16),
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 16),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
        legend.title = element_markdown(size = 14),
        
        axis.text.y.right  = element_text(colour = "#D72000FF"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_markdown(colour = "#D72000FF"),
        axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(colour = "#D72000FF"),
        axis.line.y.right  = element_line(colour = "#D72000FF"),
        
        # panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey50"),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )

p_fd_outlier_pct
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12
#| dpi: 150

design <- "
AAAA
BBBB
CCDD
CCDD
"

fig_2 <- wrap_plots(
    list(
        plot_tree_astral, plot_spacer(), p_fd_dxy_fill_fst, 
        (p_fd_outlier_pct + theme(plot.tag.position = "topright"))
    ), 
    design = design
) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") +
    plot_layout(
        guides = "collect",
```
